quote: We were gonna go with, you know, Aurora solar or something like that. But, apparently, they just filed bankruptcy.
stewart_read: Customer hands over a rich competitive/emotional data point (a failed solar company) and the rep only offers sympathy before pivoting to a referral pitch.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this a closer-tier conversation not worth setter time, but the schema flags prior-design probing as a required verify item regardless.
coaching_implication: Ask one follow-up: what was the quoted system size/price with Freedom Pros, to hand the closer a comparison point.

quote: Yeah. So it's gonna be under my my mom and dad's name. I live here with them, so the the entire program will be under their name.
stewart_read: This is a hard qualifier — program must be in the actual homeowner's name — and the rep never confirms the parents will attend or even be reachable for the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically letting the enthusiastic son drive now and planning for the specialist to sort ownership on-site, but nothing in the transcript shows that handoff being made explicit.
coaching_implication: Should have said directly: 'Since the account is in your parents' name, we'll need them on the call Saturday' rather than letting it slide.

quote: Yeah. So it's gonna be me making a decision. I mean, technically, it is my house. So that's why I'm the one that's the decision maker.
stewart_read: Customer directly contradicts his earlier statement about parents owning the home, and the rep does not reconcile it or insist the actual owners join.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive miss — the rep let this pass to keep momentum toward the close rather than stopping to resolve which household member legally qualifies.
coaching_implication: Flag for the closer explicitly: ownership status is unresolved, confirm with parents before running numbers.

quote: Yes. So how does the process work and, can you just guide me through it?
stewart_read: Customer opens with unsolicited curiosity about the process itself — a strong buying signal the rep should lean into rather than treat as a routine question.
coaching_implication: Rep answered adequately but generically; could have asked what prompted his interest (interest_question) right here to deepen the anchor — instead that section was skipped entirely.

stewart_read: Customer gives a kWh figure and the rep files it silently, moving straight to bill-photo logistics instead of reflecting it back as a hook (e.g., 'that's a solid amount of usage, let's see what solar could offset').
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically holding the number for the closer's proposal rather than editorializing on it himself, consistent with setter-scope discipline.
coaching_implication: A one-line acknowledgment ('that's a decent chunk of usage — good candidate for a real system size') would create curiosity without giving away numbers.

quote: Can you can you ping me as soon as you're on the way so that I know your ETA, and then I I can make sure I'm on home accordingly?
stewart_read: Button-up is left partial per verified events — no explicit hour-block statement, no 'is that fair?' handshake — even though the customer is engaged and asking operational questions.
coaching_implication: Close the loop with the full button-up template (hour block, no-driving, verbal handshake) even when the customer sounds bought-in — it's what protects show rate.
